335047.title: Moment-graph formula conjecture for the Poincaré polynomial of a fundamental domain
335047.statement:
Let $F_{\gamma}$ be the fundamental domain equipped with the action of $\widetilde{T}=T\times \mathbb{G}_{m}$, and let $\Gamma$ be its moment graph, with vertices $F_{\gamma}^{\widetilde{T}}$ and edges $F_{\gamma}^{\widetilde{T},1}$. For a total order $\mathfrak{o}$ on the vertices of $\Gamma$, orient every edge so that its source is greater than its target. If $n^{\mathfrak{o}}_{v}$ is the number of arrows with source $v$, define

$$
b_{2i}^{\mathfrak{o}}=\sharp\{v\in\Gamma:n^{\mathfrak{o}}_{v}=i\},
$$

and

$$
P^{\mathfrak{o}}(t)=\sum_i b_{2i}^{\mathfrak{o}}t^{2i}.
$$

Let $P(t)$ be the Poincaré polynomial of $F_{\gamma}$.

**Moment-graph formula conjecture.** One has

$$
P(t)=\min_{\mathfrak{o}}\{P^{\mathfrak{o}}(t)\},
$$

where $\mathfrak{o}$ ranges over all total orders on the vertices of $\Gamma$, and the minimum is taken with respect to the ordering in which $P_1(t)<P_2(t)$ when the leading coefficient of $P_2(t)-P_1(t)$ is positive.

This conjectural formula would recover the Poincaré polynomial of the fundamental domain from its moment graph. The statement depends on the cohomological purity framework described immediately before it, but the source gives no resolution or further evidence for the conjecture.

335047.source_review: Conjecture 1.1; source pp. 4–6, purity framework and GL2 complete-graph case. All four arXiv versions downloaded.

335270.title: Extremal conjecture for trees with bounded leaf count in bipartite graphs
335270.statement:
Let $\mathbb{T}_{k,l}$ denote the family of trees of order $k$ with the leaf parameter specified by the source, and let $ex(n,m;\mathbb{T}_{k,l})$ be the maximum number of edges in an $n$-by-$m$ bipartite graph containing no member of $\mathbb{T}_{k,l}$. Assume

$$
n\geq m,\qquad k\geq l,\qquad n\geq k,\qquad m\geq l.
$$

**Extremal conjecture for $\mathbb{T}_{k,l}$.** The following formulas hold:

1. If $k<2l-2$ and $m\geq2l$, then

$$
ex(n,m;\mathbb{T}_{k,l})=(l-1)(n+m-2l+2).
$$

2. If $k\geq2l-1$, $m-l+1\geq k-1$, and $n-m+l-1\geq k$, then

$$
ex(n,m;\mathbb{T}_{k,l})=(k-1)(m-l+1)+(l-1)(n-m+l-1).
$$

3. If $k\geq2l-1$, $m-l+1\geq k-1$, and $n-m+l-1\leq k-1$, then

$$
ex(n,m;\mathbb{T}_{k,l})=(k-1)m.
$$

The conjecture proposes exact bipartite Turán numbers in three parameter regimes. The supplied text gives no resolution evidence, and the definition of $\mathbb{T}_{k,l}$ is not included in the provided context.

335270.source_review: Conjecture 4.4 and Question 1.5. The source defines Tk,l by bipartition sizes k,l, NOT number of leaves or total order k. Source forbids failure to contain ALL trees, not containment of ANY tree.

All contained every type. Exhaustive tree-type generation and embedding checks; sampled host graphs only. Need either structured beyond-range host obstruction or full upper bound.

335436.title: Two-part Hilton–Milner conjecture for non-trivially intersecting families
335436.statement:
Let $X_1$ and $X_2$ be disjoint sets with sizes $n_1$ and $n_2$, and let ${X_1, X_2\choose k,\ell}$ denote the family of sets $F$ satisfying $|F\cap X_1|=k$ and $|F\cap X_2|=\ell$. A family is **intersecting** if any two of its members have nonempty intersection, and **non-trivially intersecting** if it is intersecting but has no element common to every member. **Two-part Hilton–Milner conjecture.** If ${\cal F}$ is a non-trivially intersecting subfamily of ${X_1, X_2\choose k,\ell}$, then

$$
|{\cal F}|\leq \max \left\{ \left( 1+{n_1-1\choose k-1}-{n_1-k-1\choose k-1}\right){n_2\choose \ell},
\left.{n_1\choose k}\left( 1+{n_2-1\choose \ell-1}-{n_2-\ell-1\choose \ell-1}\right) \right\}.
$$

This conjectures that the largest non-trivially intersecting families arise from the two constructions obtained by placing the distinguished element and the exceptional set entirely in $X_1$ or entirely in $X_2$; its status is not resolved in the source.

335437.title: Two-part cross-intersection conjecture for two-sided intersecting families
335437.statement:
Let $X_1$ and $X_2$ be disjoint sets with sizes $n_1$ and $n_2$, and let ${X_1, X_2\choose k,\ell}$ denote the family of sets $F$ satisfying $|F\cap X_1|=k$ and $|F\cap X_2|=\ell$. A family is **two-sided intersecting** if any two members intersect in both parts, equivalently their intersections with $X_1$ and with $X_2$ are nonempty. **Two-part cross-intersection conjecture.** If ${\cal F}$ is a two-sided intersecting subfamily of ${X_1, X_2\choose k,\ell}$, then

$$
|{\cal F}|\leq \max \left\{ \left( {n_2-1\choose \ell -1}-{n_2-\ell-1\choose \ell-1}\right){n_1\choose k}+1+{n_1\choose k}-{n_1-k\choose k},
\left( {n_1-1\choose k -1}-{n_1-k-1\choose k-1}\right){n_2\choose \ell}+1+{n_2\choose \ell}-{n_2-\ell \choose \ell} \right\}.
$$

The proposed extremal families combine an almost intersecting projection in one part with a pair of nonempty cross-intersecting families in the other; the source says that either this construction or its symmetric version should be largest, and gives no resolution.

335838.title: Chapoton's conjecture on Newton polygons of q-Ehrhart numerators
335838.statement:
Let $P$ be a poset on $\\{1,2,\dots,m\\}$, and let $\mathcal{O}(P)$ be its order polytope. For each $x\in P$, let $\overline{\operatorname{mc}}(x)$ be the maximum size of a chain starting at $x$, and let $a_1\le a_2\le \dots\le a_m$ be the increasing rearrangement of $\overline{\operatorname{mc}}(1),\dots,\overline{\operatorname{mc}}(m)$. Let $N_P(q,x)$ denote the numerator of the $q$-Ehrhart polynomial of $\mathcal{O}(P)$, and let $C(a_1,\dots,a_m;h)$ be the convex hull of $(0,0)$, $(a_1+\dots+a_i,i)$ for $1\le i\le m$, $(h,m)$, and $(h-m,0)$, where $h\ge a_1+\dots+a_m$. **Chapoton's conjecture.** The Newton polygon of $N_P(q,x)$ is

$$
\mathrm{Newton}(N_P(q,x))=C(a_1,\dots,a_m;h)
$$

for some integer $h\ge a_1+\dots+a_m$. The conjecture predicts a precise relation between the chain structure of a poset and the Newton polygon of the numerator of its $q$-Ehrhart polynomial; the paper's title indicates that this conjecture is proved in the source.

336775.title: Restriction of maximal separated collections to mutation-closed domains
336775.statement:
Let ${\mathcal{M}}$ be an oriented matroid on ground set $E$. A collection $\mathcal{S}\subseteq 2^E$ is **${\mathcal{M}}$-separated** when it is separated according to the oriented-matroid separation relation. A **mutation-closed domain** ${{\mathcal{D}}}\subset 2^E$ is a union of connected components of the mutation graph of ${\mathcal{M}}$.

**Restriction conjecture.** If $\mathcal{S}$ is a maximal-by-size ${\mathcal{M}}$-separated collection inside $2^E$ and ${{\mathcal{D}}}$ is a mutation-closed domain, then $\mathcal{S}\cap {{\mathcal{D}}}$ is a maximal-by-size ${\mathcal{M}}$-separated collection inside ${{\mathcal{D}}}$.

This predicts that global maximal separated collections restrict to maximum separated collections on every mutation-closed domain. The source provides no resolution of the conjecture.

338753.title: Berend et al.'s balanced knight coloring conjecture
338753.statement:
Let $n$ be a positive integer and consider an $n\times n$ chessboard. For each position $(i,j)$, let $N[i,j]$ be the closed neighborhood of the corresponding knight-move graph vertex, and let $\phi_{\mathrm{knight}}(n,n)$ denote the optimal value of the balanced black-and-white coloring integer program, namely the maximum possible value of $\min\{b,w\}$ subject to no black piece having a white piece in its closed neighborhood. **Berend et al.'s conjecture.**

$$
\phi_{\mathrm{knight}}(n,n)=\begin{cases}n\left(\frac{n-2}{2}\right)&\text{if }n\text{ is even},\
\left(\frac{n-3}{2}\right)+\frac{n-1}{2}&\text{if }n\text{ is odd}.
\end{cases}
$$

The conjecture gives the claimed optimum for balanced nonattacking black and white knight placements. The source reports that the formula is fulfilled for even $n$ but not for odd $n$, so the conjecture as stated is refuted.

339954.title: Extremal monotonicity conjecture for the side length function of regular polygon stars
339954.statement: Let $P_n$ be a regular polygon with $n$ sides, let $s_{2l+1}$ denote the side length function for inscribed $(2l+1)$-pointed stars, and call a point of $P_n$ a **midpoint crossing** or **vertex crossing** according to whether the corresponding star has a midpoint coincidence or a vertex coincidence. For $n\ge 4l+2$, **Extremal monotonicity conjecture.** Every midpoint crossing of $P_n$ is a global minimum of $s_{2l+1}$, every vertex crossing is a global maximum, midpoint and vertex crossings are interleaved around $P_n$, and $s_{2l+1}$ is strictly monotonic between adjacent midpoint and vertex crossings. This would strengthen the preceding partial characterization, which establishes that crossings are local extrema and that all crossings of each type have a common value; the conjectured global ordering and strict monotonicity remain unproved in the supplied text.

342076.title: Huang's maximum-diversity conjecture for intersecting families
342076.statement:
Let $n=2k+1$ and let $[n]=\{1,2,\ldots,n\}$. Write $2^{[n]}=\{X:X\subset [n]\}$. A family $\mathcal{F}\subset 2^{[n]}$ is **intersecting** if any two of its elements intersect. For $x\in[n]$, let $\mathcal{F}(x)=\{F:x\in F\in\mathcal{F}\}$, and define the diversity of $\mathcal{F}$ by $div(\mathcal{F})=|\mathcal{F}|-\max_{x\in[n]}|\mathcal{F}(x)|$. Let

$$
\mathcal{Q}_{k}=\{A:A\subset [2k+1],\ |A|\geq k+1\}.
$$

**Huang's conjecture.** If $\mathcal{F}\subset 2^{[n]}$ is intersecting, then

$$
div(\mathcal{F})\leq div(\mathcal{Q}_{k})=\sum_{i=k+1}^{2k}\binom{2k}{i}.
$$

The conjecture concerns the maximum possible diversity of an intersecting family of subsets of an odd-sized ground set. The paper's abstract states that it gives two intersecting families with diversity larger than the proposed bound, thereby disproving Huang's conjecture.

342803.title: Faudree–Gould–Jacobson–Lesniak–Saito conjecture on 2-factors in Hamiltonian graphs
342803.statement:
Let $k\in\mathbb{N}$, and let $G$ be a **Hamiltonian graph**, meaning a graph containing a Hamilton cycle. A **$2$-factor** of $G$ is a spanning $2$-regular subgraph, equivalently a union of vertex-disjoint cycles containing every vertex of $G$.

**Faudree–Gould–Jacobson–Lesniak–Saito conjecture.** For any $k\in\mathbb{N}$ there are constants $c_k<1/2$, $n_k$ and $a_k$ such that any Hamiltonian graph $G$ of order $n\ge n_k$ with

$$
\delta(G)\ge c_k n+a_k
$$

contains a $2$-factor consisting of $k$ cycles.

The conjecture asks whether Hamiltonicity permits a minimum-degree threshold below Dirac's bound of $n/2$ while still guaranteeing a $2$-factor with exactly $k$ cycles. The surrounding discussion presents this as a conjecture of Faudree, Gould, Jacobson, Lesniak and Saito; no resolution is supplied here.

342803.mathematical_attempts_and_remaining_gap: Take epsilon=1/4 and a_k=0. This directly proves the reserved existence of c_k<1/2. Small finite examples cannot refute unspecified n_k.

344548.title: Axis-parallel extremality conjecture for taxicab distance sets
344548.statement: Let $d,k\in\mathbb{N}$. For $P\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d$ and an $\ell^1$-distance $\lambda>0$, say that $\lambda$ **occurs in an axis-parallel direction** if there are $x\in P$ and $1\leq i\leq d$ such that $x+\lambda e_i\in P$, where $e_i$ is the $i$-th standard basis vector. If $P$ is bounded, say that $P$ is **axis-parallel** if its largest determined $\ell^1$-distance occurs in an axis-parallel direction. **Axis-parallel extremality conjecture.** If $P$ has maximal size among subsets of $\mathbb{R}^d$ determining at most $k$ distinct $\ell^1$-distances, then $P$ is axis-parallel. The same conclusion holds within the class of sets contained in an $\ell^1$-sphere in $\mathbb{R}^d$. This conjecture supplies the additional hypothesis needed for the paper's conditional approach to the optimality conjecture. Its resolution status is not established by the supplied context.

347064.title: Longest-game conjecture for the Split Smallest strategy
347064.statement:
A Zeckendorf game on $n$ consists of legal combining and splitting moves applied to the Zeckendorf decomposition of $n$. The **Split Smallest** deterministic game applies moves by splitting from smallest to largest, after which it adds consecutive indices from smallest to largest.

**Longest-game conjecture.** The longest game on any $n$ is achieved by applying splitting moves whenever possible: first adding $1$'s, then splitting from smallest to largest, and finally adding consecutive indices from smallest to largest. The source also identifies Split Smallest, which instead splits from smallest to largest before adding $1$'s and then adding consecutive indices from smallest to largest, as another candidate for a longest possible game.

The statement is presented as an earlier conjecture, while the paper describes Split Smallest as another candidate and does not report a resolution of either claim.

347324.title: Cameron–Lucchini–Roney-Dougal's conjecture on the generating graph and replacement number
347324.statement: Let $G$ be a finite group. The **generating graph** $\Gamma(G)$ has vertex set $G$, with two distinct vertices adjacent when they generate $G$. A vertex is **isolated** if it has no adjacent vertex. The replacement number $\psi(G)$ is the smallest value of $r$ for which the equivalence relations $\equiv_m$ and $\equiv_m^{(r)}$ coincide, where $x_m y$ means that $x$ and $y$ can be substituted for one another in all generating sets for $G$, and $x_m^{(r)}y$ means that they can be substituted for one another in all generating sets of size $r$. **Cameron–Lucchini–Roney-Dougal's conjecture.** If no vertex of $\Gamma(G)$ is isolated, then $\psi(G)\leq 2$. The conjecture asserts that the absence of isolated vertices forces the equivalence relation determined by all generating sets to coincide with that determined by generating sets of size at most two. Its resolution is not established by the supplied text.

347642.title: Eigenvalue sign and maximum conjecture for the perfect matching association scheme
347642.statement:
Consider the character table of the perfect matching association scheme on $2k$ vertices. For the row corresponding to the module indexed by $[2k-2\ell,2\ell]$, the greatest eigenvalue is the eigenvalue corresponding to the same class of the scheme, $[2k-2\ell,2\ell]$. In that row, all eigenvalues corresponding to classes greater than $[2k-2\ell,2\ell]$ in the dominance ordering are negative.

**Eigenvalue sign and maximum conjecture.** The greatest eigenvalue in the row indexed by $[2k-2\ell,2\ell]$ occurs in the class $[2k-2\ell,2\ell]$, and every eigenvalue in that row belonging to a strictly greater class in the dominance ordering is negative.

The conjecture concerns the signs and ordering of eigenvalues in the perfect matching association scheme, analogous to known patterns for the permutation association scheme. The paper does not provide a resolution of this claim.

348144.title: Linear-operator sumset growth conjecture
348144.statement:
Let $\mathcal{T}:\mathbb{R}^d\rightarrow\mathbb{R}^d$ be a linear operator with characteristic polynomial $f(\mathcal{T})$. For an irreducible polynomial $g\in\mathbb{Z}[x]$ dividing $f(\mathcal{T})$, define

$$
H(g)=\prod_{i=1}^m(|a_i|+|b_i|),
$$

where $g(x)=\prod_{i=1}^m(a_i x+b_i)$ is a full complex factorization. If no polynomial $g$ with rational coefficients divides $f(\mathcal{T})$, the minimum below is defined to be infinity. **Linear-operator sumset growth conjecture.**

$$
\lim_{n\rightarrow\infty}\min_{A\subset\mathbb{R}^d,\ |A|=n}\frac{|A+\mathcal{T}A|}{|A|}=\min_{g\mid f(\mathcal{T}),\ g\in\mathbb{Z}[x]}H(g),
$$

where the minimum is over all irreducible divisors $g$ of $f(\mathcal{T})$. This generalizes the preceding algebraic-multiplier claim from scalar multiplication by an algebraic number to linear operators, and the supplied source gives no resolution.
348144.review_depth: literal record and primary source passages; additional proof bodies as described

381599.title: The strong product conjecture for Grundy domination
381599.statement:
Let $G$ and $H$ be graphs. Their strong product $G\boxtimes H$ has vertex set $V(G)\times V(H)$, with two vertices $(g_1,h_1)$ and $(g_2,h_2)$ adjacent when either $g_1=g_2$ and $h_1$ is adjacent to $h_2$ in $H$, $g_1$ is adjacent to $g_2$ in $G$ and $h_1=h_2$, or $g_1$ is adjacent to $g_2$ in $G$ and $h_1$ is adjacent to $h_2$ in $H$. The parameter $\gamma_{gr}(G)$ denotes the Grundy domination number of $G$. **Strong product conjecture.** For any graphs $G$ and $H$,

$$
\gamma_{gr}(G \boxtimes H) = \gamma_{gr}(G)\gamma_{gr}(H).
$$

The inequality $\gamma_{gr}(G \boxtimes H)\geq\gamma_{gr}(G)\gamma_{gr}(H)$ is known, so the conjecture asserts the reverse inequality and would determine the Grundy domination number of every strong product from those of its factors. Its status is not resolved in the supplied source.

381866.title: Bean's discriminant-area maximality conjecture for binary forms
381866.statement:
Let $F$ be a binary form of degree $n$ with complex coefficients and nonzero discriminant $D_F$. Let $M_n$ be the maximal value of $|D_F|^{1/(n(n-1))}A_F$ over all such forms. For a real invertible matrix $M\in\operatorname{GL}_2(\mathbb R)$, write $F_M(x,y)=F(ax+by,cx+dy)$ when $M=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}a&b\\c&d\end{smallmatrix}\right)$, and say that two forms are equivalent under $\operatorname{GL}_2(\mathbb R)$ if one is obtained from the other in this way.

**Bean's conjecture.** The maximum is attained precisely when $F$, up to multiplication by a complex number, is equivalent under $\operatorname{GL}_2(\mathbb R)$ to $F_{n,n}$. In particular,

$$
M_n=D_{F_{n,n}}^{1/(n(n-1))}A_{F_{n,n}}.
$$

This conjecture is cited by the source as a conjecture of Bean and is described as naturally complementing the preceding lower-bound conjecture. No resolution is given in the supplied text.

402113.title: Conlon–Lee conjecture on extremal numbers of bipartite graphs
402113.statement: Let $H$ be a bipartite graph such that in one of the parts all the degrees are at most $r$ and $H$ does not contain $K_{r,r}$ as a subgraph. Then there exists some $\elta>0$ such that $$\operatorname{ex}(n,H)=O\!\left(n^{2-1/r-\delta}\right).$$
